Chats may expose server-published live canvases through an observable provider-neutral collection when the owning provider permits canvas presentation for that session. Each chat discovers membership from its advertised canvas channel references; each subscribed channel supplies presentation metadata and an optional live HTTP(S) source. Unknown membership is distinct from an authoritative empty collection, and pending canvas state retains its resource without a source. Registered canvas-definition listings use the same distinction: `undefined` means the provider registry is unsettled and consumers retain the last authoritative listing, while an empty array authoritatively clears it. A provider that returns `undefined` must publish another canvas change after the registry settles so consumers request the authoritative snapshot. Agent Host providers enable presentation only for durable Copilot sessions; ephemeral sessions expose no canvas capability. Remote sessions expose it only while browser remote proxying is enabled, unless their host is known not to proxy browser connections, so a temporary disconnect keeps their canvases. Canvas execution and presentation continue to follow the existing canvas enablement setting. Session and chat switches suspend presentation while retaining the live browser model, so returning reattaches the same page and browser-side state. Closing presentation dismisses that canvas lifetime without invoking provider operations; archive, deletion, authoritative membership removal, or source replacement releases its browser model. Closing the canvas itself is a separate user operation that names the canvas by its channel. The Agents Window routes it through `ISessionsManagementService` to the owning provider, and the Editor Window through the chat's canvas context; either way the host ends that live canvas and notifies its canvas provider, and the resulting authoritative membership removal releases the presentation. Metadata and source updates do not reopen a dismissed canvas; a later successful model request to open that instance explicitly permits revealing the existing lifetime again. Open-request identity is derived from the owning chat's tool state and is client-only presentation metadata, not a canvas-channel revision. Canvas membership, sources, and browser models are not persisted across restarts. The workbench owns the shared canvas editor, presentation lifecycle, and retained browser models; the Agents Window supplies its active-session/active-chat context, editor working sets, and layout policy, while the Editor Window permits exact owners represented by visible chat widgets.

-A user can pin a live canvas to the Agents Window sidebar. `IPinnedCanvasService` (`contrib/canvases`) keeps each pin live through the optional provider hook `observeCanvas`, routed through `ISessionsManagementService`, which observes one canvas channel without the active-session gate; holding that reference may keep the owning session resident, so pins are capped. The canvas stays owned by its chat, whose agent keeps driving it. Pins persist only identity (provider, session, chat, extension, canvas type, instance ID, and last title) in workspace storage and rebind by instance ID. Activating a pin always shows its canvas page and never the owning chat; a pin that is not connected reconnects through the optional provider hook `observeChatCanvases`, which observes the chat's canvas membership without the active-session gate until the pin binds. A pin is removed when its session is removed or archived, its chat is deleted, or `ISessionsManagementService.onDidCloseCanvas` reports its canvas closed; closing its tab keeps it. A pinned canvas is shown full-page on the canvas custom view and never opens as an editor in another chat's working set: `ICanvasService.isOwnerPresentable` still governs editors, while `isPresentable` also admits a canvas that the canvas page shows. One canvas view at a time attaches a browser model; a hidden view never takes it from a visible one.

Activating a pin always shows its canvas page and never the owning chat; a pin that is not connected reconnects through the optional provider hook `observeChatCanvases`, which observes the chat's canvas membership without the active-session gate until the pin binds. A chat can lose a canvas it had open, for example when a lazily activated canvas provider stays dormant after an Agent Host restart, so when a shown pin's chat lacks its canvas, the pin asks the chat to open that instance again through `ISessionsManagementService.openCanvas` and binds once the chat publishes it; if the chat cannot open it or does not publish it in time, the pin shows as unavailable until it is shown again. A request made through a session that goes away or is replaced is abandoned and made again once the session returns. A pinned canvas is shown full-page on the canvas custom view and never opens as an editor in another chat's working set: `ICanvasService.isOwnerPresentable` still governs editors, while `isPresentable` also admits a canvas that the canvas page shows. One canvas view at a time attaches a browser model; a hidden view never takes it from a visible one.

Recorded GitHub issue and pull request artifacts are resolved from `ISession.artifacts` independently of workspace or repository availability, alongside repository-discovered associations. Chat-scoped surfaces use records owned by the focused chat plus unowned session records, while session-wide consumers use the aggregate; repository associations follow the focused chat's workspace or the session workspace respectively. Recorded references never enter the dedicated pull request and issue pills, even when a provider echoes them into its GitHub metadata; they always stay in the references pill. A chat's pull request pill shows the pull requests of its folders' repositories; recorded pull requests from other repositories remain in the artifacts list. The dedicated pills, artifact de-duplication, and pull-request polling share this resolution. Promoted entries retain their optional recorded-reference ID; presentation uses that ID for per-item removal, names the removal after whether the record is an artifact or a reference, and never infers record identity from a title or URL.
